title: Proper is finite near a finite fibre (retained with the author's slogan block): for f : X -> S proper with S locally Noetherian and the set-theoretic fibre over s finite, some open neighbourhood V of s has f^{-1}(V) -> V finite.

core_obligations: Locate the quasi-finite locus and its openness.
Use properness to push the complement's image away from s.
Verify the restriction is quasi-finite with finite fibres over the shrunk base.
Conclude finiteness via the proper-with-finite-fibres characterization.

difficulty_reason: The neighbourhood argument is complete in the span: a finite fibre makes f quasi-finite at all points above s (morphisms-lemma-finite-fibre); the quasi-finite locus U is open (morphisms-lemma-quasi-finite-points-open); its complement Z has closed image since f is proper, so some V through s avoids f(Z); over V the restriction is locally quasi-finite and proper, hence quasi-finite (locally-quasi-compact lemma), has finite fibres (quasi-finite lemma), and is therefore finite by this chapter's characterization card L16381.

dedup.scope: Neighbourhood finiteness of proper maps at finite fibres; consumed by cards L16372 (ample-in-neighbourhood sleight of hand) and L16396 (algebraize-morphism).
